Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space and let
$T:V\to V$ be an endomorphism. The endomorphism $T$ is **self-adjoint** when

$$T^*=T,$$

and **normal** when

$$TT^*=T^*T,$$

where $T^*$ is the adjoint from
[[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]].

Every self-adjoint endomorphism is normal, because $TT^*=T^2=T^*T$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space, let
$T:V\to V$ be linear, and let $\mathcal E$ be an orthonormal basis of $V$. Write

$$A=[T]_{\mathcal E}^{\mathcal E}.$$

Then:

1. $T$ is self-adjoint if and only if $A=A^*$.
2. $T$ is normal if and only if $AA^*=A^*A$.

Over $\mathbb R$, $A^*$ is just $A^{\mathsf T}$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space, let $T:V\to V$ be
self-adjoint, and let $v\in V$ be nonzero. The **Rayleigh quotient** of $v$ for
$T$ is

$$R_T(v):=\frac{\langle Tv,v\rangle}{\langle v,v\rangle}.$$

Because $\langle v,v\rangle>0$ for nonzero $v$ in an inner product space, this
quotient is a well-defined real number.

Let $T:V\to V$ be self-adjoint on an $n$-dimensional real inner product space,
and list its eigenvalues in weakly decreasing order:

$$\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_n.$$

Then for every $1\le k\le n$,

$$\lambda_k=\min_{\dim W=n-k+1}\ \max_{0\ne v\in W} R_T(v)=\max_{\dim U=k}\ \min_{0\ne v\in U} R_T(v).$$

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space and let $T:V\to V$ be
self-adjoint. Then $V$ has an orthonormal basis consisting of eigenvectors of
$T$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner product space and let $T:V\to V$
be linear. Then $T$ is normal if and only if $V$ has an orthonormal basis
consisting of eigenvectors of $T$.

If $W$ is a subspace of a finite-dimensional real or complex inner product space $V$, then

$$V=W\oplus W^\perp.$$

Thus every $v\in V$ has unique vectors $w\in W$ and $z\in W^\perp$ with $v=w+z$.

derivations.claim: Suppose $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$. By [F2], $A$ represents a self-adjoint endomorphism in the standard orthonormal basis, and [F3] identifies its Rayleigh quotient with $q_A$. Taking $k=m$ in [F4] gives $\lambda_{\min}=\min_{\dim W=1}\max_{x\in W\setminus\{0\}}q_A(x)$. On each one-dimensional $W$, homogeneity gives the same quotient for every nonzero vector, and every nonzero $x$ spans such a $W$; hence this minimum is exactly $\min_{x\ne0}q_A(x)$. By [F5], write $x=\sum_j c_ju_j$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis with real eigenvalues $\lambda_j$; then $q_A(x)=\sum_j\lambda_jc_j^2/\sum_jc_j^2$, which equals $\lambda_{\min}$ exactly when every nonzero coefficient belongs to the least-eigenvalue eigenspace.

Suppose $\mathbb F=\mathbb C$. By [F2], $A$ represents a self-adjoint endomorphism in the standard orthonormal basis; by [F1] this endomorphism is normal, so [F6] gives an orthonormal eigenbasis $u_1,\ldots,u_m$. Every eigenvalue is real because if $Au_j=\lambda_j u_j$, then $\overline{u_j^*Au_j}=u_j^*A^*u_j=u_j^*Au_j$, so $\lambda_j\|u_j\|^2$ is real and $\|u_j\|^2>0$. For $x=\sum_j c_ju_j\ne0$, the quotient is the weighted average $\sum_j\lambda_j|c_j|^2/\sum_j|c_j|^2$, so it is at least the least eigenvalue and equals it exactly when all nonzero coefficients lie in its eigenspace.

In either field, the least eigenspace is nonzero, so [F7] gives a unique orthogonal decomposition of each vector into its $E_{\min}$ and $E_{\min}^{\perp}$ parts; define $P_{\min}$ to be the first component. Uniqueness makes $P_{\min}$ linear, since sums and scalar multiples of decompositions are the corresponding decompositions. At least one $P_{\min}e_j$ is nonzero, since otherwise linearity and the fact that the standard vectors span $\mathbb F^m$ would imply $P_{\min}=0$, contradicting $E_{\min}\ne\{0\}$. The first such $j$ is uniquely determined by the fixed basis order. Normalize this projection. Over $\mathbb C$, its first nonzero coordinate $z$ is changed to $|z|>0$ by multiplication by $\overline z/|z|$; over $\mathbb R$, multiplication by $z/|z|$ makes that coordinate positive. $$\lVert T\rVert:=\max\{\lVert Tv\rVert:\lVert v\rVert=1\}.$$

The next theorem proves that this maximum exists and equals the largest
singular value.

For vectors $u,v$ in a real or complex inner product space,

$$|\langle u,v\rangle|\le\lVert u\rVert\lVert v\rVert.$$

Equality holds if and only if $u$ and $v$ are linearly dependent, including the case in which either vector is zero.

Fix a field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, an order $d\ge2$, and positive physical dimensions $n_1,\ldots,n_d$. The finite coefficient space is the tensor-array space $\mathcal H=\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with the Frobenius pairing and lexicographic index conventions of [[def-finite-tensor-arrays-and-frobenius-inner-product]]. A **normalized finite state** is an array $\psi\in\mathcal H$ with $\|\psi\|_F=1$.

An **open-boundary matrix-product state (MPS), or tensor train (TT), presentation** is a TT core list from [[def-tensor-train-cores-bond-ranks-and-canonical-gauges]] with $r_0=r_d=1$ whose contraction is $\psi$. In particular, each core has shape $r_{k-1}\times n_k\times r_k$ and the shared internal indices are summed.

A **periodic MPS presentation** consists of positive integers $r_0,\ldots,r_d$ with $r_d=r_0$ and matrices $A_k^{(i_k)}\in\mathbb F^{r_{k-1}\times r_k}$ for each $1\le i_k\le n_k$. It represents the array
$$\psi_{i_1,\ldots,i_d}=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(A_1^{(i_1)}A_2^{(i_2)}\cdots A_d^{(i_d)}\right).$$
A finite MPS/TT state is a normalized array admitting at least one of these exact presentations; a presentation need not be unique or canonical.

A **finite Hermitian Hamiltonian input** is a linear endomorphism $H:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$ whose matrix in the standard lexicographic basis satisfies $H^*=H$, where $*$ is conjugate transpose as in [[def-finite-tensor-arrays-and-frobenius-inner-product]]. This page uses only that finite-dimensional Hermitian input and makes no claim about how a physical model assembles it. For nonzero $\psi$, its Rayleigh energy is
$$\mathcal E_H(\psi)=\frac{\langle\psi,H\psi\rangle_F}{\|\psi\|_F^2};$$
for a normalized state this equals $\langle\psi,H\psi\rangle_F$.

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ with $d\ge2$. A tensor-train (TT) representation consists of integers $r_0=r_d=1$, internal bond sizes $r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$, and cores
$$ G_k\in\mathbb F^{r_{k-1}\times n_k\times r_k}\quad(1\le k\le d) $$
such that
$$ A_{i_1,\ldots,i_d} =\sum_{\alpha_1=1}^{r_1}\cdots\sum_{\alpha_{d-1}=1}^{r_{d-1}} G_1(1,i_1,\alpha_1)G_2(\alpha_1,i_2,\alpha_2)\cdots G_d(\alpha_{d-1},i_d,1). $$
An empty bond index set gives an empty sum, hence the zero tensor; in particular, all internal bond sizes zero represent zero. A bond size $r_k$ is the storage dimension contracted between cores $k$ and $k+1$. The cut-$k$ unfolding groups modes $1,\ldots,k$ against $k+1,\ldots,d$ as fixed in [[def-finite-tensor-arrays-and-frobenius-inner-product]].

For an internal bond $k$, an invertible matrix $S\in\mathbb F^{r_k\times r_k}$ gives a gauge transformation by replacing the two adjacent cores with
$$ \widetilde G_k(\alpha,i,\beta)=\sum_{\gamma=1}^{r_k}G_k(\alpha,i,\gamma)S_{\gamma\beta}, \qquad \widetilde G_{k+1}(\beta,j,\eta)=\sum_{\gamma=1}^{r_k}(S^{-1})_{\beta\gamma}G_{k+1}(\gamma,j,\eta). $$
Their contraction is unchanged because $\sum_\beta S_{\gamma\beta}(S^{-1})_{\beta\gamma'}=\delta_{\gamma,\gamma'}$.

The left matricization of core $G_k$ has row index $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and column index $\alpha_k$. The core is left-isometric if this matrix $L_k$ satisfies $L_k^*L_k=I_{r_k}$. The right matricization has row index $\alpha_{k-1}$ and column index $(i_k,\alpha_k)$; the core is right-isometric if its matrix $R_k$ satisfies $R_kR_k^*=I_{r_{k-1}}$. A TT is in mixed canonical gauge about core $\ell$ when cores $k<\ell$ are left-isometric and cores $k>\ell$ are right-isometric.

Hence every array entry is unchanged, and the TT bond at cut $k$ has $r_k r_0$ possible pair indices.

The d=2 boundary case is explicitly covered in step 1.1 with an empty middle-core clause.

derivations.claim: Let $M\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$ be any core matricization. Scan its columns in order, starting with an empty list and retaining a column exactly when it is not in the span of those already retained. At termination the retained columns are independent, and every skipped column lies in their final span; hence they span the column image of $M$ and their count is $q=\operatorname{rank}(M)$ by [F2]. If $q>0$, apply [F4] to obtain a matrix $Q$ with orthonormal columns spanning those retained columns; their Gram–Schmidt coordinates form an upper triangular $R_{11}$ with nonzero diagonal. If $q=0$, then $M=0$ and use the empty factorization.

Move the retained column indices to the front by a permutation $\Pi$. Every remaining column lies in the span of $Q$, so it equals $Q$ times its coordinate vector $Q^*$ applied to that column. Thus $M\Pi=Q[R_{11}\ R_{12}]$ for some $R_{12}$, with $Q^*Q=I_q$; equivalently $M=QB$ where $B=[R_{11}\ R_{12}]\Pi^*$. This is an exact rank-revealing thin QR factorization for every rectangular shape.

Starting at the left boundary, apply step 2.1 to each left matricization of cores $1,\ldots,s-1$. Replace the current core matricization $M$ by $Q$ and absorb $B$ into the next core. Since $M=QB$, the shared-index contraction in [F1] is unchanged; $Q^*Q=I_q$ makes the replaced core left-isometric by [F3]. Induction over the swept cores gives the required left-isometric prefix.

Starting at the right boundary, apply step 2.1 to the adjoint $M^*$ of each right matricization of cores $d,\ldots,t+1$. If $M^*\Pi=QB$, then $M=\Pi B^*Q^*$. Replace the current right matricization by $Q^*$ and absorb $\Pi B^*$ into the preceding core. The shared-index contraction in [F1] is unchanged, and $Q^*Q=I_q$ makes the replaced matricization right-isometric by [F3]. Induction gives the right-isometric suffix and preserves the represented array, while leaving cores $k<s$ untouched. If $t<d$, the final absorption into core $t$ can change the contracted center coefficients; if $t=d$, there is no right sweep.

The scan drops only columns already in the span of retained columns, so each bond dimension changes only from its former size to the exact matrix rank. If any swept matricization had rank zero, that core would be zero and the full TT contraction would be zero, contrary to the nonzero-state hypothesis; hence every reduced swept bond has positive dimension. Steps 3.1 and 3.2 establish the exact mixed canonical gauge.

Work in exact arithmetic over a fixed field $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and order $d\ge2$. The inputs are:

- a normalized finite MPS/TT state $\psi\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ together with one concrete presentation of $\psi$, either an open-boundary TT core list or periodic trace matrices; the supplied presentation must contract to $\psi$;
- a finite Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$ on that same tensor-array coefficient space;
- a positive integer sweep budget $M$;
- a window width $w\in\{1,2\}$; and
- optionally, positive integer rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}$.

The procedure is the following.

1. If the supplied presentation is in periodic trace form, convert it exactly to the open-boundary TT form using [[lem-na-periodic-mps-to-open-tt]]. Otherwise take the supplied open-boundary core list. Keep the resulting open-boundary core list.

2. For each of $M$ full sweeps, perform one forward pass and one backward pass. For width $w$, the windows are the $d$ single sites when $w=1$, or the $d-1$ adjacent site pairs when $w=2$. Visit them in increasing order in the forward pass and decreasing order in the backward pass.

3. Before each window update, place the TT in mixed canonical gauge about that window using the deterministic rank-revealing QR sweeps of [[lem-na-mixed-canonical-qr-gauge-preserves-state]]. Contract the fixed left and right cores to form the isometric center embedding $E$ and compute the finite effective matrix $H_{\mathrm{eff}}=E^*HE$.

4. Apply the exact ground-vector rule of [[lem-na-finite-hermitian-ground-vector-with-deterministic-tie]] to $H_{\mathrm{eff}}$. Let $x$ be the resulting unit eigenvector and replace the center coefficient vector by $x$. Record its local Rayleigh energy $x^*H_{\mathrm{eff}}x=\lambda_{\min}$ and residual $\|H_{\mathrm{eff}}x-\lambda_{\min}x\|_2$.

5. For a two-site window, reshape the updated center as a matrix with row index (left bond, first physical index) and column index (second physical index, right bond). Compute an exact compact SVD $X=U\Sigma V^*$. In a forward pass replace the first core by the reshape of $U$ and absorb $\Sigma V^*$ into the second core. In a backward pass absorb $U\Sigma$ into the first core and replace the second core by the reshape of $V^*$. Retain every positive singular direction, so this split changes no tensor entries. For a one-site window, keep that site as the center.

6. After each complete forward/backward sweep, if rank caps were supplied, apply [[alg-tensor-train-rounding]] to the current TT and record its cut tails $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_{d-1}$ and $\tau=(\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}\delta_k^2)^{1/2}$. If $\tau<1$, normalize the rounded tensor and continue from it. If $\tau\ge1$, discard that rounded candidate, retain the last normalized unrounded tensor, and record status **rounding-skipped**. If no rank caps were supplied, do not round.

Return the final normalized TT state, the energy and local-residual records, all accepted discarded-tail records, and status **budget-complete** or **rounding-skipped** according to whether any requested rounding was skipped.

Let $\psi_0=Ex_0$ be a normalized finite MPS in mixed canonical gauge about a one-site or two-site center, with $\|x_0\|_2=1$. Let $H_{\mathrm{eff}}=E^*HE$ be its effective Hermitian matrix, and replace the center by the deterministic unit ground vector $x_* $ of $H_{\mathrm{eff}}$, giving $\psi_*=Ex_*$. Then $\psi_*$ is normalized and
$$\mathcal E_H(\psi_*)\le\mathcal E_H(\psi_0).$$
This claim is before any bond truncation.

Work in exact arithmetic over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. The input is a valid TT core list for a tensor of order $d\ge2$ and exactly one of rank caps $c_1,\ldots,c_{d-1}\in\mathbb N_0$ or absolute tail tolerances $\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_{d-1}\in[0,\infty)$.

1. **Left orthogonalize without truncation.** For $k=1,\ldots,d-1$, reshape core $G_k$ into a matrix with rows $(\alpha_{k-1},i_k)$ and columns $\alpha_k$. Compute an exact compact SVD $M=U\Sigma V^*$, replace $G_k$ by the reshape of $U$, and absorb $\Sigma V^*$ into the next core along their common bond. Omitting zero singular directions is exact. The resulting cores $G_1,\ldots,G_{d-1}$ are left-isometric.

2. **Truncate from right to left.** For $k=d,d-1,\ldots,2$, reshape the current $G_k$ into a matrix $M_k$ with rows $\alpha_{k-1}$ and columns $(i_k,\alpha_k)$, and compute an exact compact SVD $M_k=U_k\Sigma_kV_k^*$. If its positive singular values are $\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_s>0$, choose $q_{k-1}=\min(c_{k-1},s)$ for rank caps, or the least $q_{k-1}\in\{0,\ldots,s\}$ with $\sum_{j>q_{k-1}}\sigma_j^2\le\tau_{k-1}^2$ for tolerances. Record $\delta_{k-1}=(\sum_{j>q_{k-1}}\sigma_j^2)^{1/2}$. Replace $G_k$ by the reshape of the first $q_{k-1}$ rows of $V_k^*$ and absorb $U_{k,1:q}\Sigma_{k,1:q}$ into the previous core.

If $q_{k-1}=0$, the represented tensor becomes zero; set all remaining internal ranks to zero and their unperformed tails to zero. If the input represents zero, return the all-zero-rank representation and zero tails immediately. The output is the rounded core list and all recorded cut tails. No finite-precision error guarantee is part of this exact-arithmetic procedure.

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$, $d\ge2$, and let $A^{\langle k\rangle}$ denote its cut-$k$ unfolding. For sequential TT-SVD, let $r_k$ be its retained bond size and $\delta_k$ its discarded singular-value tail at cut $k$. For rounding, let the input TT represent $A$ and use the same notation for the output bond sizes and recorded tails. Then both procedures satisfy
$$ \|A-\widehat A\|_F^2\le\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}\delta_k^2. $$
If no positive singular value is discarded, the output is exactly $A$. In full-rank TT-SVD, $r_k=\operatorname{rank}(A^{\langle k\rangle})$ for every cut, and these are the minimal possible TT bond sizes among exact representations.

Let $\mathcal H=\mathbb F^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}$ be a finite tensor-array space over $\mathbb F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $H:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H$ be self-adjoint, and let $\psi,\phi\in\mathcal H$ satisfy $\|\psi\|_F=\|\phi\|_F=1$. Then
$$\left|\langle\psi,H\psi\rangle_F-\langle\phi,H\phi\rangle_F\right|\le 2\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|\psi-\phi\|_F.$$

The function induced by an inner product satisfies, for all vectors $u,v$ and scalars $\lambda$,

$$\lVert v\rVert\ge0,\qquad \lVert v\rVert=0\Longleftrightarrow v=0,$$

$$\lVert\lambda v\rVert=|\lambda|\lVert v\rVert,\qquad \lVert u+v\rVert\le\lVert u\rVert+\lVert v\rVert.$$

Let $V$ be a normed space. For all $x,y\in V$,
$$\bigl|\|x\|-\|y\|\bigr|\le \|x-y\|.$$
In particular, the norm map is $1$-Lipschitz for the norm metric.

derivations.claim: There are finitely many local updates in the sweep. Each exact local solve preserves normalization and weakly decreases energy by [F2]; each intervening exact SVD split preserves the represented tensor and therefore its norm and energy by [F1]. Induction over this finite sequence shows that every intermediate state stays normalized and its energy does not exceed the preceding one. Hence $\mathcal E_H(\psi_*)\le\mathcal E_H(\psi_0)$.

The tails $\delta_k$ are those recorded by [F3]. By [F4], $e:=\|\psi_*-\widetilde\psi\|_F\le\tau$. The triangle inequality [F6] gives $1=\|\psi_*\|_F\le e+\|\widetilde\psi\|_F$, so $\|\widetilde\psi\|_F\ge1-e\ge1-\tau>0$ and $\phi$ is defined.

By [F7], $|1-\|\widetilde\psi\|_F|\le e$. Also, homogeneity [F6] and $\phi=\widetilde\psi/\|\widetilde\psi\|_F$ give $\|\phi-\widetilde\psi\|_F=|1-\|\widetilde\psi\|_F|$. Therefore $\|\phi-\psi_*\|_F\le\|\phi-\widetilde\psi\|_F+\|\widetilde\psi-\psi_*\|_F\le2e\le2\tau.$

Apply [F5] to the unit states $\phi$ and $\psi_*$ to get $\mathcal E_H(\phi)\le\mathcal E_H(\psi_*)+4\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}\tau$. Combine this with step 1.1 to obtain the claimed bound relative to $\psi_0$. The same inequality gives the asserted upper bound on any post-rounding increase.

Step 1.1 uses finitely many updates and exact finite SVDs; local tie choices are deterministic by the algorithm.
